blocks.text: Architectural facade design for a barbershop, Kyiv, Ukraine

parts.html: A barbershop facade in Kyiv: we developed the architectural design for the facade reconstruction and produced the 3D visualization. The brief was to make the shop visible from the street and keep the facade in line with the barbershop’s brand identity without clashing with the neighboring buildings. The visualizations show the facade in its street context, with the sidewalk, trees and adjacent buildings.

The main material is white stone with gray veining. It clads the ground-floor wall, the wide cornice above the shop windows and the column by the entrance. We made the base below the windows from dark stone: street dirt shows less on it, and it visually anchors the windows from below.

A wide three-section glazed front in thin dark frames runs along the street. Through the glass you can see the interior and the shelves with warm lighting, so in the evening the window works as a sign. To its left is a separate display window in a glowing golden frame. It holds a single large object and gives the facade a second focal point.

The entrance is on the corner, under a canopy. Inside the portal the walls are clad in dark stone, the double glass door is set back, and on either side of it are wall sconces that light up and down. Wide steps with white treads and dark risers lead up to the door. The side of the portal is glazed, so the shop window is visible from the entrance. In front of the entrance is a patch of lawn with a tree in a stone curb.

The name sits on the cornice in raised, edge-lit letters. Below it, a thin line of light runs the full length of the facade, separating the cornice from the shop windows in the evening. Apart from this line and the sconces by the door, the facade is lit only by the shop windows and the illuminated window frame.
Work like this for commercial premises is part of our architecture and design service: facade concept, material selection, entrance and signage design, and visualizations for approval.
